name: The five categories of the Pāśupatas (pañcārtha)

definitions.definition: The whole teaching is summed up as effect (kārya), cause (kāraṇa), union (yoga), rule (vidhi) and the end of suffering (duḥkhānta), all implied in the first sūtra.
Śaṅkara reports the same five as taught by Paśupati for release from the paśus' bond, and rejects the accompanying view of the Lord as merely efficient cause.
Everything dependent on the Lord: the knowledge-qualities of souls (vidyā), the insentient parts (kalā) and the souls (paśu); eternal but produced, favoured and concealed by the Lord in play.
The Lord (Pati) alone is the independent cause who emits, maintains, withdraws and favours the effect; he acts by will and play, not by dependence on karma.

name: Yoga as union of self and Lord

definitions.definition: Yoga is the conjunction of the self with the Lord through the mind; in action (muttering, meditation on Oṃ in the heart) or in the cessation of action; it arises for one of unclouded mind who practises.

name: The rule (vidhi): observance and its aids

definitions.definition: Activity producing merit: primary - the observance (vows and the six doors) - and secondary - re-bathing and the like; it begins with ash, has censure in the middle and ends with feigned folly, and has three limbs, gift, worship and austerity.

Liberation, reached by the Lord's grace: impersonal (absolute cessation of suffering) and personal (the Lord's powers of knowing and acting); it is union with and proximity to Rudra, from which there is no return.
Yāmuna reports it as mere absolute cessation of pain (opponent's report).

relations.note: Kauṇḍinya sets the Pāśupata lordship beyond others' isolation

name: The paśu (bound soul) in the Pāśupata system

definitions.definition: All conscious beings but the Lord, with or without bodies, including gods and those liberated by Sāṃkhya-Yoga; bound by the kalās; their bondage is lack of lordship.

name: The kalās: ten effects and thirteen instruments

definitions.definition: The insentient parts that bind the soul: ten effects (earth, water, fire, air, space; sound, touch, form, taste, smell) and thirteen instruments (five knowledge-senses, five action-organs, buddhi, ahaṃkāra, manas).
A quality of the paśu: cognitive (discriminating - called citta - or not) or non-cognitive (merit and demerit).

name: The powers of the Pāśupata yogin

definitions.definition: Powers arise with yoga: distant seeing, hearing, thinking, knowing and omniscience (power of knowing); swiftness of mind, taking forms at will, acting without organs (power of acting); and eight marks of perfection - subject to none, not to be entered, not to be slain, fearless, imperishable, unaging, deathless, unobstructed. They arise gradually after six months of constant yoga and make the yogin a chief of Mahādeva's troops. The texts present them as signs and as part of liberation, not as dangers.
The Skanda Purāṇa tells of Pāśupata siddhas who went to Śiva's abode in the same body.
Hostile dramas attribute flight and power over gods and heavens to Kāpālikas.

name: The nine groups: eight pentads and one triad

definitions.definition: The Gaṇakārikā sums the system as gains, impurities, means, places, stages, purifications, factors of initiation and strengths (five each) plus three livelihoods; the teacher is the knower of these nine groups.

name: The five stages of Pāśupata practice (avasthā)

definitions.definition: Manifest (vyakta: the sign shown, in the temple), unmanifest (avyakta: sign hidden, courting dishonour among people), conquest (jaya: of the senses, in cave or empty house), cutting (cheda: in the cremation ground), completion (niṣṭhā: all activity ceased, in Rudra).
Teacher, people, cave (or empty house), cremation ground and Rudra - the places of the five stages in order.
Kauṇḍinya's list: the dwelling, the world, the empty house, the cremation ground, Rudra.

False knowledge, demerit, the cause of attachment, falling away and the root of the paśu-state (Gaṇakārikā); Kauṇḍinya: ignorance, demerit, habituation to objects, non-attainment of steadiness, lack of lordship.
Knowledge, austerity, permanence (constant union with the god), steadiness and perfection (Gaṇakārikā); Kauṇḍinya: knowledge, austerity, constant union with the god, yoga, arising of the qualities.
Residence (with the teacher, i.e. the faculties of learning), observance, muttering and meditation, constant remembrance of Rudra, and grace.
The absolute removal of each of the five impurities.
Devotion to the teacher, clarity of mind, conquest of opposites, merit and vigilance.

Material (knowledge of disciple and teacher, the ritual items, the brahmin disciple), time (forenoon), rite, image and teacher; initiation is by ash consecrated with the five mantras before the southern image.
Alms (stages 1 and 3), discarded food (stage 2), whatever is obtained (stage 4); none in stage 5.

name: Courting dishonour and the exchange of merit and sin

definitions.definition: The second-stage ascetic hides his sign and provokes contempt; those who revile him receive his demerit and he receives their merit; dishonour is the highest restraint and makes his austerity complete. Kauṇḍinya: undertaken only after gaining knowledge, with impurity reduced and the teacher's leave, without breaking the restraints.
Feigned snoring, trembling, limping, amorous gestures, senseless acts and senseless speech - 'doors' through which dishonour brings merit and removes demerit.
The Pāśupata initiate leaves the rules of his former āśrama for the restraints of a state beyond the four āśramas; open to brahmins of any āśrama.
Yāmuna objects that Śaivas devise āśramas outside the Vedic order.
The Lord produces the effect as he wills, all at once or in sequence, depending neither on karma nor on the soul; karma bears fruit only when favoured by his will.
Rejected: a Lord who distributes unequal lots independently would be partial; the Lord's creation depends on beings' karma (BS 2.1.34), and a merely efficient Lord is inconsistent (BS 2.2.37).
Perception, inference and scripture (the teaching from Maheśvara through the teachers); other alleged means are included in these.

name: Teacher and disciple in the Pāśupata tradition

definitions.definition: The disciple is a tested brahmin of good family, keen senses and desire to know, who seeks the end of suffering, not dharma, wealth, pleasure or isolation; the teacher acts from grace, knows the nine groups and consecrates; one with scripture but without faith or knowledge of the groups is a pseudo-teacher.
The teachers from Lakulīśa to Rāśīkara saluted daily (Ratnaṭīkā); eighteen are named by Jain doxographers; the Mathurā inscription counts ten generations from Kuśika to 380 CE.

name: The incarnation of Śiva as Lakulīśa

definitions.definition: The tradition's accounts: Śiva enters an abandoned corpse in a cremation ground and becomes the brahmacārin Lakulī at Kāyāvatāra, with four disciples (Liṅga P.); the Lord in a brahmin's body descends at Kāyāvataraṇa and teaches Kuśika at Ujjayinī (Kauṇḍinya); Śiva is born to Viśvarūpa and Sudarśanā, enters the body of the dead infant, and at last merges into the Brahmeśvara liṅga at Kāyāvarohaṇa (Kāravaṇa-māhātmya).

notes: Scholarly dating (c. 2nd c. CE) is kept on tch:lakulisa as labelled metadata.

definitions.definition: In each Dvāpara of the Vaivasvata manvantara Śiva incarnates as a yoga-teacher with four disciples; the twenty-eighth and last is Lakulīśa/Nakulīśa at Kāyāvatāra.

name: Death and the final stage in Pāśupata practice

definitions.definition: In the fourth stage the ascetic lives in the cremation ground until the body falls, remembering Rudra; the fifth stage is without body, its place Rudra himself; the liberated brahmin does not return.
Dying at Kāyāvarohaṇa leads to Rudra's world (Kūrma P.).

name: The Lord's play as the ground of creation

definitions.definition: The Lord's activity is play: in play he produces, favours and conceals the effect; the teacher's activity is for grace.
Sadyojāta, Vāmadeva, Aghora, Tatpuruṣa and Īśāna, closing the five adhyāyas, muttered daily as the five purifiers.
Yamas: non-harming, celibacy, truthfulness, non-dealing, non-stealing; niyamas: non-anger, service of the teacher, purity, light diet, vigilance - all ten counted as yamas.

relations.note: a parallel five-and-five scheme; members differ (asaṃvyavahāra, akrodha, guruśuśrūṣā, āhāralāghava, apramāda)

name: Śaivism's two great divisions: Atimārga and Mantramārga

definitions.definition: The Śaiva scriptures distinguish the Atimārga - knowledge 'beyond the world', whose followers are not re-created - from the Mantra path, in whose Śiva-knowledge all Atimārga goals are attained with ease.
Worldly, Vedic, spiritual (Sāṃkhya-Yoga), Atimārga and Mantra, in ascending order.

Pāśupatas ('beyond the āśramas') and Lākulas ('beyond the world', skull observance) in the Niśvāsamukha; the Svacchanda names skull-observers and Pāśupatas, and levels for Mausulas, Kārukas, Vaimalas and 'Pramāṇa'; the Kūrma lists Pāśupata, Soma and Lākula; some sources and scholars add the Kāpālikas (Somasiddhānta) as a third division.

name: The great vow of the skull (mahāvrata)

definitions.definition: Living as a Kapālin with a skull-bowl and skull-staff, in imitation of Bhairava's penance for Brahmā's head; by it a man becomes an ascetic (as reported).
The Lākula observance 'beyond the world' with skull and khaṭvāṅga.

name: Bhairava's severing of Brahmā's head and the skull-penance

definitions.definition: Śiva as Bhairava cuts off Brahmā's fifth head, wanders as the skull-bearer to expiate brahmin-murder, and is freed at the holy tīrtha; remembering his skull-bearer's guise destroys sin.
Ear-ornament/necklace, rucaka, earrings, crest-jewel, ash and sacred thread, with skull and khaṭvāṅga as sub-insignia; knowing and wearing them is claimed to prevent rebirth (opponents' report).

name: Rival accounts of liberation: transfer, possession, production, manifestation

definitions.definition: Liberation is the manifestation of the soul's own Śiva-nature, not transfer, possession or production of the Lord's qualities.
The Pāśupatas speak of the attainment of the Lord's qualities and powers in liberation.

notes: Which Atimārga school held which of the rejected views is a scholarly attribution, not stated in the passage.

name: Kālāmukha monasteries, assemblies and royal preceptors

definitions.definition: Temple-based maṭhas (chief among them the Kōḍiya-maṭha at Balligāve) grouped in the Śakti- and Siṃha-pariṣads, their pontiffs learned in many systems and serving as rājagurus; the maṭhas fed, taught and healed.

name: Levels assigned to Atimārga goals by the Mantramārga

definitions.definition: Pāśupatas reach the Aiśvara level; Mausulas and Kārukas the Māyā principle; Vaimalas the level of Tejeśa; the 'Pramāṇa' the Dhruva; skull-observers and Pāśupatas are not re-created.

name: The four Māheśvara schools of the doxographers

definitions.definition: Vācaspati: Śaivas, Pāśupatas, Kāruṇika-siddhāntins, Kāpālikas.
Yāmuna and Rāmānuja: Kāpālikas, Kālāmukhas, Pāśupatas, Śaivas.
Guṇaratna: Śaivas, Pāśupatas, Mahāvratadharas, Kālamukhas.
